technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Cloud Netflix Eureka for service discovery in modules and admin server.
Implement Service Provider Interface (SPI) pattern to abstract controller implementations for deployment flexibility.
Leverage Spring Boot Actuator and Spring Integration for metrics capture and persistence.
Utilize CI/CD tools (e.g., Jenkins or GitHub Actions) for automated builds, testing, and Docker image uploads.
Adapt existing Spring XD FTP modules to s-c-s architecture, ensuring compatibility with Java 17+ and Spring 6.0.

Eureka server is already configured and available for registration.

activities.activity_description: Initialize the project structure, configure build tools (e.g., Maven/Gradle), and add dependencies for Spring Boot, Eureka, and other required libraries.
Implement Eureka client in s-c-s modules to register and update their current state with Eureka for discovery, as per user story U1.
Configure and implement self-registration of the xd-admin server with Eureka to expose it as a discoverable endpoint, as per user story U4.
Refactor ContainersController, StreamsController, ModulesController, and JobsController to use SPI calls for deployment-based invocation, as per user story U2.
Develop direct capture of module metrics using Spring Integration channels and Spring Boot Actuator APIs, exploring existing options, as per user story U3.
Implement persistence of module metrics using Spring Boot's export API with Redis as default storage, allowing for snapshot intervals, as per user story U7.
Port FTP source modules from Spring XD to the s-c-s repository, ensuring they function correctly as source modules in streaming pipelines, as per user story U6.
Setup continuous integration builds for s-c-s projects to automatically build and test code commits, as per user story U5.
Configure CI workflow to build, bundle, and upload the module-launcher Docker image to DockerHub under the Spring Cloud location, as per user story U8.
